name: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
authors: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, et al. (Stanford University; SambaNova Systems; UC Berkeley). Equal contribution: Qizheng Zhang (Stanford), Changran Hu (SambaNova).
venue: ICLR 2026 (arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.04618, submitted Oct 2025); also appears on OpenReview (forum eC4ygDs02R).
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (a dedicated LLM 'Reflector' role critiques Generator trajectories to distill insights from successes and errors); feedback can be tool-verified (code execution success/failure) or ground-truth-label-guided depending on availability.
feedback_source: Mixed: self-generated natural-language reflection plus external execution feedback (code execution success/failure in agent tasks, formula correctness). Can optionally use ground-truth-oracle labels (offline/with-GT-labels setting); notably ACE also works WITHOUT labeled supervision by leveraging natural execution feedback.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine: Generator produces trajectories, Reflector iteratively critiques (up to 5 refinement rounds), Curator merges delta updates; offline adaptation runs over multiple epochs (up to 5); online adaptation updates context sequentially per test sample. Incremental delta updates rather than monolithic rewrite.
reflection_object: prompt/context (the evolving 'playbook' context made of itemized bullets). ACE reflects on the agent's action trajectory and reasoning to extract reusable strategies, domain concepts, and failure modes, which are then written as structured context entries. It modifies the input context, not model weights.
requires_training: none (no weight updates; pure context/prompt adaptation at inference/adaptation time).
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge: a Reflector LLM (same base model, DeepSeek-V3.1 non-thinking, for fairness) serves as the critic that judges trajectories and extracts lessons; improvement signal can also come from verifiable execution feedback (code success/failure) and optionally ground-truth labels. No separately trained reward model.
distillation_target: prompt / playbook-cheatsheet: reflection is distilled into a structured, evolving context (a 'playbook' of itemized bullets with metadata and helpful/harmful counters). This functions as a curated prompt/agent-memory artifact rather than model weights.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: ACE is an engineered modular agentic scaffold (Generator/Reflector/Curator with delta updates and grow-and-refine), in the lineage of Reflexion and Dynamic Cheatsheet; reflective behavior is built into the framework, not RL-emergent.
memory_type: playbook/cheatsheet (structured context of itemized 'bullets'); used both as offline system prompt and online agent memory. Each bullet has metadata (unique id, helpful/harmful counters) and content (reusable strategy, domain concept, or failure mode).
memory_persistence: cross-task (and cross-episode): context accumulates and is reused across samples/tasks. Offline adaptation builds a context on the training split reused at test; online adaptation evolves memory sequentially across the test stream.
memory_curation_mechanism: overwrite/evolution via incremental delta updates plus a grow-and-refine principle: new bullets are appended with new ids while existing bullets are updated in place (e.g., incrementing helpful/harmful counters); periodic de-duplication (semantic-embedding-based) and pruning control redundancy, performed by lightweight non-LLM merging logic. Explicitly designed to avoid 'context collapse' from monolithic rewriting.
error_localization_granularity: step-level / itemized: insights and corrections are localized to individual context 'bullets' (delta entries) rather than rewriting the whole context; the Reflector attributes which specific bullets/strategies were helpful or misleading within a trajectory.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: ACE transfers accumulated experience (reusable strategies, domain concepts, failure modes) across tasks/samples via the evolving context, in the spirit of Reflexion/ExpeL/Dynamic Cheatsheet; it also supports within-stream online refinement.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-oriented: lessons (including recorded failure modes) are written into the context so future tasks avoid past pitfalls; updates happen per-sample (online) or per-epoch (offline) rather than as mid-trajectory in-flight correction.
task_domains: tool-use / agentic (LLM agents interacting with apps and APIs) and domain-specific reasoning (financial analysis with XBRL).
benchmarks: AppWorld (autonomous agent tasks: API understanding, code generation, environment interaction; test-normal and test-challenge splits; metrics TGC/SGC); FiNER (XBRL token labeling, 139 entity types); Formula (XBRL numerical-reasoning extraction). HotpotQA and Game of 24 discussed as cases where ACE is less beneficial.
headline_result: On AppWorld (DeepSeek-V3.1 base), ReAct+ACE reaches 59.4% average (offline, +17.0 over 42.4 ReAct baseline) and matches top-ranked IBM CUGA (GPT-4.1-based, 60.3%) on the leaderboard while surpassing it on the harder test-challenge split, despite using a smaller open-source model. Overall +10.6% average over baselines on agents and +8.6% on finance.
baselines: Base LLM (ReAct for AppWorld); In-Context Learning (ICL, few/many-shot); MIPROv2 (DSPy prompt optimizer, auto='heavy'); GEPA (reflective Genetic-Pareto prompt optimizer); Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC, online adaptive memory); top-ranked production agent IBM CUGA (GPT-4.1) for leaderboard comparison.
gains_vs_baseline: Agents (AppWorld): +10.6% average over baselines; offline ReAct+ACE beats ReAct+ICL by 12.3% and ReAct+GEPA by 11.9%; online beats Dynamic Cheatsheet by 7.6%; up to +17.1% over ReAct without ground-truth labels. Finance (FiNER+Formula): +8.6% average with GT labels; offline beats ICL/MIPROv2/GEPA by 10.9% avg; online beats DC by 6.2%; e.g. Formula offline 67.5->85.5 (+18.0).
compute_cost_profile: Substantially cheaper than monolithic-rewrite optimizers due to incremental delta updates and non-LLM merge/de-dup. Offline AppWorld: 82.3% lower adaptation latency and 75.1% fewer rollouts vs GEPA. Online FiNER: 91.5% lower adaptation latency and 83.6% lower token dollar cost vs Dynamic Cheatsheet. Produces longer contexts than GEPA but without linear inference-cost/GPU-memory increase.
known_limitations: Relies on a reasonably strong Reflector; if it fails to extract meaningful insights, the context can become noisy or harmful. Effectiveness depends critically on feedback quality: without reliable signals (GT labels or execution outcomes) both ACE and DC can degrade and the context may be polluted by spurious signals (e.g., FiNER without labels: -3.4). Not all tasks need rich contexts (HotpotQA, Game of 24 benefit from concise instructions); ACE is most useful where detailed domain knowledge, complex tool use, or env-specific strategies are required.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: task-dependent: in agent tasks works with external-tool/execution feedback (intrinsic, no oracle labels needed, +14.8% without GT); in domain-specific (finance) tasks it largely requires oracle-label/ground-truth or reliable signals, degrading without them. So it spans self-verify -> external-tool/verifier -> oracle-label depending on domain; feedback reliability is the discriminating variable.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / requires reliable feedback: net-positive under rich feedback (agent execution signals, formula correctness), but can be net-negative when feedback is absent or unreliable (e.g., online FiNER without labels -3.4, DC without labels -3.7). Does not require ground-truth labels for agent tasks but does benefit from them for finance.
calibration_effect: not-measured (paper does not report confidence calibration / overconfidence effects).
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (qualitatively): the Reflector identifies recurring pitfalls/common failure modes and records them as context bullets; bullets carry helpful/harmful counters tracking which strategies misled the agent. Not a formal failure-attribution benchmark method.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets brevity bias (optimization collapsing to short generic prompts that drop domain insights) and context collapse (monolithic LLM rewriting abruptly erasing accumulated knowledge, e.g. AppWorld context dropping from 18,282 tokens/66.7% acc to 122 tokens/57.1% acc in one step). Records domain-specific failure modes and tool-use pitfalls; addresses superficial/lossy self-reflection by separating reflection from curation.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released; uses existing AppWorld, FiNER, Formula. Authors release the LLM prompts used for ACE and baselines for reproducibility (Appendix D). Code release not confirmed.
builds_on: Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al. — adaptive test-time memory, the agentic architecture ACE builds on); Reflexion (verbal reflection on failures); GEPA (reflective Genetic-Pareto prompt evolution); TextGrad (textual 'gradient' prompt optimization); MIPROv2/DSPy (prompt optimization); A-MEM (agentic memory entries); ReAct (agent scaffold/base implementation); ICL (in-context learning).
extended_by_or_inspired: As a recent (Oct 2025) paper accepted to ICLR 2026, it has rapidly become a reference for context-engineering / self-improving-agent and agent-memory work; ~181 citing works per Google Scholar. Specific named direct successors not individually confirmed from a fetched source. [uncertain]
citation_count: approximately 181 (Google Scholar, 'Cited by 181' for the main arXiv entry, as of June 2026; a separate Scholar citation cluster lists 23). Semantic Scholar count not retrievable (API rate-limited).
reasoning_model_native: No / not-native: ACE is an external scaffold applied around a base model (DeepSeek-V3.1 in non-thinking mode); it does not target o1/R1-style built-in reflection. It is complementary to reasoning models but its reflection comes from the engineered Reflector role, not the model's internal reasoning.
on_policy_distillation_link: Related conceptually: ACE distills the model's own on-policy execution trajectories (Generator outputs) and their natural execution feedback into a reusable context/playbook artifact (a form of experience/skill distillation), but uses no weight updates or policy gradients; it is a context-level analogue to on-policy skill distillation rather than parameter-space distillation.
sample_efficiency: High relative to optimizers: achieves gains with up to 5 epochs / max 5 Reflector refinement rounds and batch size 1, using 75.1% fewer rollouts than GEPA on offline AppWorld; GEPA itself is noted as needing up to 35x fewer rollouts than RL. Exact minimal-sample threshold not isolated.
